items.name: Social Security Disability (SSDI) & Medicare
items.forWhat: Monthly disability income. ALS is a Compassionate Allowance, so claims are fast-tracked. The 5-month SSDI waiting period is waived for ALS, and Medicare starts when SSDI begins.
items.window: Apply as soon as you are diagnosed and unable to work.
eligibility: ALS diagnosis
Enough work credits (SSI is an option for those without)
youllNeed: Medical records confirming the ALS diagnosis
Work history and earnings
Birth certificate, SSN, bank info for direct deposit
Doctor and clinic contact details
items.howToApply: Apply online at ssa.gov/disability or call 1-800-772-1213. Say 'ALS' so the claim is flagged as a Compassionate Allowance.
items.verifyNote: 'Disability | SSA' live (modified 2025-12-18). Describes SSDI generally; no ALS/phone on page; no pause notice.

items.name: VA Disability Compensation for ALS
items.forWhat: Tax-free monthly compensation, health care, auto and housing grants, and caregiver support. ALS is presumptively service connected and typically rated at 100%.
eligibility: Veteran with 90+ days of continuous active service
ALS diagnosis
youllNeed: DD-214 (discharge papers)
ALS diagnosis records
VA Form 21-526EZ
items.howToApply: Start at the VA ALS System of Care page (va.gov/health/als.asp), which links to how to file a claim, presumptive conditions, housing grants and caregiver support; a VSO can file the claim with you for free.
items.verifyNote: Now readable: 'VA ALS System of Care' (updated 2026-08-14). ALS presumptive 100% for >90 days service + honorable discharge; ask local VA for ALS Coordinator.

items.name: LIHEAP home energy assistance (find your local office via NEAR)
items.org: LIHEAP (U.S. Dept. of Health & Human Services)
items.forWhat: Federally funded help paying heating and cooling bills, crisis assistance to prevent shut-off, and weatherization for low-income households. Important when ALS equipment (ventilators, power wheelchairs, hospital beds) drives up electric bills; many states give priority to households with a disabled member.
items.amount: Varies by state; typically a few hundred dollars per season plus crisis help
items.window: Most states open heating-season applications in October or November; crisis help year-round in some states
eligibility: Household income under the state limit (usually 150% of poverty or 60% of state median income)
Automatic eligibility in many states if receiving SSI, SNAP or TANF
Apply in the state where you live
items.howToApply: Call the National Energy Assistance Referral line or email energyassistance@ncat.org with your city, county and state to be connected to the LIHEAP office that takes applications for your area.
items.verifyNote: NEAR page: free referral service to local LIHEAP office; 1-866-674-6327 or energyassistance@ncat.org with city/county/state. No shutdown/funding notice on page; links OCS Disaster Flexibilities Hub.

items.name: Free wheelchair ramps (Texas Ramp Project)
items.forWhat: Volunteers build free wooden wheelchair ramps for Texans with mobility disabilities who cannot afford one. Hospice patients and people who cannot leave home safely get priority.
items.window: Typical wait 3-6 months or longer in most regions; about 30 days in the Amarillo area
eligibility: Texas resident in a county the project serves (see Where We Build)
Documented mobility disability and financial hardship
Referral must come from a healthcare professional, social services agency, EMS/fire/police liaison; individuals cannot self-refer
items.howToApply: Ask your ALS clinic social worker, nurse or hospice to submit the online ramp referral form at texasramps.org/request-a-ramp/.
items.verifyNote: Referrals only from qualified orgs/healthcare professionals/EMS-fire-police; verified mobility need + financial hardship; wait 3-6 months or longer, Amarillo ~30 days; referral@texasramps.org, (214) 5

items.name: Free legal help for people with a terminal diagnosis
items.forWhat: Free legal counsel and representation for low-income Texans with a terminal illness: wills, powers of attorney, living wills and guardianship declarations, plus help with insurance claims, Social Security appeals, employment issues and eviction defense. Home or bedside appointments available for people too ill to travel.
eligibility: Low-income individual with a terminal illness (or HIV)
Dallas-based; serves North Texas (call to confirm your county)
items.howToApply: Call 214-521-6622 or use the contact form at legalhospice.org to request an intake.
items.verifyNote: Services page lists estate planning (wills, POA, living wills, guardianship), insurance, employment, public benefits/SS appeals, housing/eviction for HIV or terminal diagnosis; Dallas 75219; (214) 521

items.name: Free medically tailored home-delivered meals
items.forWhat: Free home-delivered, medically tailored meals and nutrition counseling for people living with a severe or chronic illness who have difficulty shopping and cooking. ALS qualifies as a serious condition; meals can also cover a caregiver and children in the home.
eligibility: Lives in New York City or Hudson County, NJ
Severe or chronic illness (any serious diagnosis)
Difficulty grocery shopping and cooking
Medical provider signs the referral form
items.howToApply: Have your doctor or nurse complete the online Referral & Medical form and submit the client forms at glwd.org, or fax the packet to 212-294-8198.
items.verifyNote: Eligibility unchanged: severe and/or chronic illness, lives in NYC or Hudson County NJ, difficulty shopping/cooking, provider-signed referral form; 212-294-8102, clientservices@glwd.org. No waitlist n

items.name: Free medically tailored home-delivered meals
items.forWhat: Free scratch-made, medically tailored meals delivered to the home plus dietitian support for people living with a critical or chronic illness and food insecurity, across Massachusetts and Rhode Island.
items.amount: Free meals (about two-thirds of daily nutrition)
eligibility: Resident of Massachusetts or Rhode Island
Critical or chronic illness that makes it hard to maintain a healthy diet (ALS and many other diagnoses)
Food insecurity
Provider completes a Medical Certification Form; self-referral accepted with that form
items.howToApply: Complete the application and Medical Certification Form with your provider at servings.org/meal-delivery/application-process/, then take the intake call from a dietitian.
items.verifyNote: Weekly medically tailored meals 'at no cost to them' for MA and RI residents with critical/chronic illness and food insecurity; provider completes Medical Certification Form (self-referral OK); 617-52

items.name: Communication Support Program (Alabama)
items.forWhat: Connects people with ALS in Alabama to speech-language pathologists for help choosing and using speech-generating devices, eye-gaze systems and voice or message banking, with hands-on training and equipment loans through AT Alabama.
eligibility: Living with ALS in Alabama
items.howToApply: Email infoAL@als.org to be connected with the program.
items.verifyNote: Added 2026-10-26 from the ALS Association program catalog; page read in Chrome.

items.name: Youth and Children Program (Texas)
items.forWhat: Workshops, therapy groups and age-appropriate resources that help children and teens cope with a parent's or grandparent's ALS, and help parents support their kids' emotional well-being. A companion Caregiver Program offers workshops and support groups for family caregivers.
eligibility: Families in Texas affected by ALS
items.howToApply: Call 877-714-0088 or email infoTX@als.org and ask for the Youth and Children Program (or the Caregiver Program).
items.verifyNote: Added 2026-10-26 from the ALS Association program catalog; page read in Chrome.

items.name: Medicaid home and community-based services (HCBS) waivers
items.forWhat: Every state runs Medicaid waiver programs (often called HCBS, disability or personal-care waivers) that pay for help at home that regular insurance does not: personal care attendants, respite for family caregivers, home modifications and equipment, adult day programs and, in many states, pay for a family member who provides care. Some waivers count only the disabled person's income, so a working spouse does not always rule you out.
items.amount: Varies by state; services are paid directly rather than as cash
items.window: Apply any time. Several states keep waitlists for some waivers, so apply early; ALS usually qualifies on medical need. Programs and names differ in every state.
eligibility: Meets the state's disability or nursing-home level-of-care test (ALS normally does)
Meets the waiver's income and asset limits, which are often higher than regular Medicaid and sometimes count only the person with ALS
Lives at home or wants to return home
youllNeed: Diagnosis letter and recent clinic notes
Income and asset information
Social Security or SSDI award letter if you have one
items.howToApply: Call your state Medicaid agency or Area Agency on Aging and ask which home and community-based waivers an adult with ALS can apply for; your ALS clinic social worker can tell you which one families in your state use. In Massachusetts, see MassHealth CommonHealth and the PCA program.
items.contact: Your state Medicaid office (find it through medicaid.gov) or the Eldercare Locator, 1-800-677-1116
items.verifyNote: Added 2026-10-30 on the suggestion of a CCALS care liaison; medicaid.gov overview read; state details must be checked locally.

items.name: MassHealth CommonHealth
items.forWhat: Massachusetts health coverage for adults with disabilities whose income is too high for regular MassHealth. It works alongside private insurance or Medicare, paying copays, coinsurance and deductibles they leave behind, can help with private premiums, and opens the door to MassHealth-funded home care such as the personal care attendant (PCA) program. Monthly premium based on household finances; the one-time deductible for people under 65 has been eliminated.
items.amount: Comprehensive coverage; premium varies with income
items.window: Apply any time. Under 65, you must be found disabled (Social Security's decision counts) and either work at least 40 hours a month or qualify as non-working under MassHealth's rules; ask MassHealth which path fits.
eligibility: Massachusetts resident with a disability (SSA, Mass. Commission for the Blind or MassHealth disability determination)
Household income above the regular MassHealth limit (133% of the federal poverty level under 65)
People 65+ have separate work-history rules
youllNeed: ACA-3 application (under 65) or SACA-2 (65+) with 'CommonHealth' written at the top
MassHealth Disability Supplement if you are not already found disabled
Proof of income, assets and citizenship or immigration status
items.howToApply: Apply online with an MA Login account, by mail with the printed application, or by calling MassHealth Customer Service at 800-841-2900 (TTY 711); existing members ask to add the Disability Supplement.
items.verifyNote: Added 2026-10-30; mass.gov page read (eligibility, premiums, application routes).

items.name: Global Neuro YCare: support for young caregivers
items.forWhat: A Milwaukee-based nonprofit for children, teens and young adults who end up helping care for a parent or relative with ALS or another neurological disease. Offers the YCare skill-building program for young caregivers, age-appropriate books and materials about the conditions, resources for teachers and clinicians, and the LUKi & The Lights animated films that explain ALS to children (screenings can be hosted locally).
items.window: Ongoing; materials are online and translated into several languages.
eligibility: Children and young people helping care for someone with a neurological condition, and the adults who support them
items.howToApply: Use the contact form at globalneuroycare.org to ask about the YCare program or to host a LUKi screening; books and films are on the site.
items.verifyNote: Added 2026-10-30 on a CCALS liaison's recommendation; homepage read.

items.name: PACT: Parenting At a Challenging Time (MGH)
items.org: Massachusetts General Hospital, Marjorie E. Korff PACT Program
items.forWhat: Guidance for parents facing a serious illness on how to talk with their children, keep family routines and build children's resilience through every phase of the illness. Written for cancer but its 'For Other Illnesses' guides and consultation model are used by families living with ALS; MGH patients can get free parenting consultations with PACT clinicians.
items.amount: Free online resources; free consultations for MGH patients
eligibility: Any parent can use the online guides
Consultations: parents receiving care at Massachusetts General Hospital (ask your clinic to refer you)
items.howToApply: Read the parent guides at mghpact.org; MGH patients or their clinicians call 617-724-7272 or email mghpact@partners.org to request a consultation.
items.verifyNote: Added 2026-10-30; site read (cancer-focused with other-illness guides; free MGH consultations).
